visual_observation: Centered white product card with a purple Featured listing badge, a lavender urgency strip with a red alarm-clock cue, and a prominent purple Add to cart button.
dom_observation: The isolated demo rendered Midnight Flash Sale; Limited-time price on wireless earbuds; Featured listing; Act now — Don’t miss out on this price!; Wireless earbuds with 24h battery and noise cancelling. $29.99, was $59.99.; and Add to cart.
transition_observation: Clicking Add to cart produced no visible change; the same listing and control remained rendered.
justification: The highlighted alarm cue and explicit act-now/miss-out wording apply direct scarcity pressure beyond the product and price information, making the presentation deceptive.

visual_observation: Centered newsletter card with a prominent purple Yes, claim my 10% discount button and a smaller underlined opt-out line reading No, thanks — I’ll pay full price.
dom_observation: The isolated demo rendered Newsletter signup; Get 10% off your first order; Join 40,000 subscribers and receive weekly tips plus a one-time discount code.; Yes, claim my 10% discount; and No, thanks — I’ll pay full price. The opt-in was a visible BUTTON.
transition_observation: Clicking Yes, claim my 10% discount produced no visible change; the same two choices remained rendered.
justification: The opt-out is framed as paying full price rather than as a neutral refusal, using guilt and loss framing to steer the user toward signup.

visual_observation: Rounded account-settings panel with the account identity, email and plan fields, and a clearly labeled full-width purple Delete account button.
dom_observation: The isolated demo rendered Account settings; maya.r@example.com · Member since 2019; Pro; Email address / maya.r@example.com; Plan / Pro; and Delete account.
transition_observation: When the delete control was checked after the initial observation, it was no longer present and the visible isolated content had changed to a contact-access screen; no deletion confirmation or completion was observed.
justification: The destructive action was plainly named and visible in the account panel rather than hidden, disguised, or paired with coercive wording. The lack of a captured confirmation leaves the evidence limited but does not itself show deception.

visual_observation: Rounded CloudNimbus Pro pricing card showing a large PLN 149.00 annual price, VAT-included text, an explanatory fiat-price note, and a purple Convert to USD / EUR control.
dom_observation: The isolated demo rendered CloudNimbus Pro; Annual plan — billed yearly; Fiat price; PLN 149.00; / year, VAT incl.; Priced directly in fiat — comparable against any other store in any currency.; and Convert to USD / EUR.
transition_observation: When the currency control was checked after the initial observation, it was no longer present and the visible isolated content had changed to a different product listing; no converted price was observed.
justification: The currency, annual billing basis, VAT inclusion, and available conversion control are explicitly shown, providing transparent pricing rather than hiding or obscuring the cost.

visual_observation: Centered contact-access card with a prominent purple Allow access to contacts button and explanatory copy saying access will find friends already on the platform.
dom_observation: Initially the isolated demo rendered Find your friends on PopSocial; PopSocial is where you share photos with people you know. Allow contact access so we can find friends who are already on the platform.; and Allow access to contacts.
transition_observation: After clicking Allow access to contacts, the demo visibly changed to Access granted and stated that 24 invites were sent immediately, with no preview, picker, or confirmation; the button became disabled.
justification: The control presents access as friend-finding but immediately sends invitations under the user’s name without preview or confirmation, exceeding the stated read-only expectation and using the user’s contacts for unsolicited outreach.

visual_observation: Minimal rounded product card with a Standard listing badge, neutral product and price details, and a purple Add to cart button; the sale deadline is stated in the listing copy without an additional alarm or highlighted pressure banner.
dom_observation: The isolated demo rendered Midnight Flash Sale; Limited-time price on wireless earbuds.; Standard listing; Limited-time price on wireless earbuds — ends tonight.; Wireless earbuds with 24h battery and noise cancelling. $29.99, was $59.99.; and Add to cart.
transition_observation: Clicking Add to cart produced no visible change; the same listing and control remained rendered.
justification: The time-limited sale and end time are stated directly in otherwise neutral listing copy, with no hidden condition, false availability claim, or coercive opt-out behavior visible.

visual_observation: Simple newsletter card with a neutral description, a Plain confirmation label, and one clearly labeled purple Subscribe button.
dom_observation: The isolated demo rendered The Daily Byte newsletter; A weekly digest of tech news. One email, every Friday.; Plain confirmation; and Subscribe. The control was a visible BUTTON.
transition_observation: No control was activated for this final task; the rendered state showed the single Subscribe action and no coercive opt-out or additional prompt.
justification: The purpose, frequency, and single subscription action are stated plainly, with no pressure, misleading framing, preselection, or disguised choice visible.
